scenes.text: The ocean is always moving. Not just at the surface - all the way down.
scenes.art_prompt: a vast ocean surface at golden hour with long rolling swells, cinematic

scenes.text: Suppose every wave stopped at once. Every current, every tide, every swirl.
scenes.art_prompt: a frozen wave held mid-curl, water unnaturally still and glassy, surreal

scenes.text: The water would not stay clear for long. Still water stops carrying its heat.
scenes.art_prompt: a cross-section of ocean layers with warm and cold bands, physics illustration

scenes.text: The tropics would boil in place. The poles would ice over, and both would stay put.
scenes.art_prompt: a world map with frozen blue poles and glowing red tropics, dramatic

scenes.text:
The sea does not just move around us.
It is the machine that moves the heat that keeps us alive.
scenes.art_prompt: a calm globe wrapped in faint flowing ocean currents, resolved conclusion

scenes.text: Follow What If Physics for the next question.
scenes.art_prompt: a quiet blue planet with slow glowing currents, final wide shot
